cases.name: Anti-RE
cases.summary: A catalogue of anti reverse-engineering techniques — anti-debug, anti-VM and runtime integrity checks — built to see evasive payloads from both sides of the debugger.

fields.label: Target
fields.value: Windows PE binaries, x86-64. A reference implementation rather than a single payload.

fields.label: Vector
value: Anti-debug via PEB.BeingDebugged, NtQueryInformationProcess, hardware breakpoint registers.
Anti-VM through CPUID hypervisor bits, registry artefacts and timing skew.
Runtime integrity: checksumming its own .text section to catch patches.

fields.label: Why
fields.value: Each check abuses an assumption the analyst makes — that the debugger is invisible, that a VM looks like bare metal, that the mapped image equals the file on disk. Break one and the payload branches to a decoy path.

fields.label: Outcome
fields.value: Hardened red team payloads against the same tooling used to analyse them.

cases.name: NoTrust Agent
cases.summary: Zero-trust posture agent for macOS. Continuous attestation and conditional access, built to test the claim that a managed endpoint is trustworthy by default.

fields.label: Target
fields.value: macOS endpoints. The companion gadget targets iOS; both assume the device may already be compromised.

fields.label: Model
value: Post-compromise persistence: signing state, launch agents and daemons, TCC grants.
Integrity drift: SIP status, unsigned kernel extensions, modified system binaries.
Trust boundary failure: a device that passes one check once, then drifts.

fields.label: Approach
fields.value: Continuous evidence over point-in-time scoring. Signals are re-collected on an interval and aggregated into a verdict that gates access — not a single enrolment check.

fields.label: Open
fields.value: An agent cannot be trusted to police its own host — a compromised one can lie. The fix is remote attestation, which is the part still unsolved.

testpoint.code: // true for one shape of input function check(s) { let h = 0x2f ; for ( const c of s) h ^= c.charCodeAt( 0 ); return h === 0 && s.length === 4 ; }
testpoint.solution: The accumulator starts at 0x2f and XORs every byte, so you need b1 ^ b2 ^ b3 ^ b4 === 0x2f . Pick any three bytes and the fourth is forced: for abc it is 0x2f ^ 0x61 ^ 0x62 ^ 0x63 = 0x4f — the character O , so abcO passes.
